post.title: Makepad Engine Monorepo
post.hook: A Rust UI engine whose physics port beat Rapier on 8 of 9 scenes
post.summary: A large Rust checkout of the Makepad UI and game framework, with apps, AI backends, a map data stack and a pure-Rust Box3D physics port that benchmarks ahead of Rapier.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Makepad is a Rust-first, cross-platform UI runtime with a live-editable DSL, GPU 2D and 3D rendering, and a studio app for running and inspecting projects. This checkout is the whole workspace: about 6000 files, 99.2% Rust, with apps, examples and vendored libraries.

## What is in it
- **Director**: an environment for watching and directing AI work through live terminals, editors and agent lanes.
- **Asset server**: a standalone daemon so the asset catalog outlives any single window, serving the VJ, sandbox and workers.
- **VJ app**: audio stem separation (BS-RoFormer, 527 MB) and Whisper karaoke timing (1.6 GB), installed from inside the app.
- **Geodata**: bulk open data for a Netherlands-first map stack, one .mbtiles per layer, including 11.4M buildings.
- **Box3D**: a std-only Rust port of Erin Catto's Box3D physics engine, with 147 tests at the initial port.

## Why the physics port matters
The README benchmarks it against Rapier on identical scenes, single-threaded, on Apple Silicon. The default build with a checked-in PGO profile is faster on eight of nine scenes, about +33% geomean for Rapier's extra time. It lands within roughly 7% of the hand-tuned C original while keeping bit-exact cross-architecture determinism and zero external crates.

## Results
Rapier's one win is washer (16844 ms against 21742 ms for box3d). On the mesh heavy tree scenes, Rapier takes 302 to 1404 ms against 171 to 594 ms.

## Open questions
Git history is a single commit from 2026-09-18, a batch of ten fixes for moving an app onto current dev, so the evolution of the work is not visible. READMEs for fab, raytrace and several libs are one liners, and Linux support for the VJ is described as untested.
